title: Watercolour strokes are transparent, pool darker at their edges, bloom and layer where they overlap
goal: The watercolour brush behaves like real watercolour: strokes are transparent washes that dry darker at their edges, bleed and bloom where wet paint touches wet paint, granulate into the paper, and build up in glazes where strokes overlap. How wet the brush is and how far it bleeds are its own settings.
notes:
Umbrella: a-brush-tool-paints-with-realistic-charcoal-chal (the user's ask, 2026-10-24). Design: docs/design/brushes.md, read it first; its decisions are settled unless this task's runner finds one cannot work, in which case they say so in the log and in the doc.

Design doc decision 4: follow Curtis et al. 1997 (wet-area mask, pigment flow, edge darkening, backruns) simplified to interactive rate; Rebelle and Fresco are the behaviour to match. Expect a Core Image or Metal kernel in PhotonzRender. Replay must stay deterministic (strokes are data and re-render on load). Wet-on-wet needs to know which earlier strokes are still wet: use stroke time (a stroke dries a few seconds after it ends, by its Wetness), recorded as data so replay matches.
acceptance: A single stroke is a transparent wash with a darker edge where the pigment pooled
Two overlapping strokes layer: the overlap is a deeper glaze, and painting into a stroke that is still wet blooms outward
Wetness and Bleed each visibly change the stroke (sheet of strokes per setting in the audit)
Measured bars the round tip fails: edge-to-centre darkness ratio of a stroke, and how far a wet stroke spreads past its painted path
Painting stays smooth at 12 MP (frame time while painting measured in the audit), and a walk with no flags paints two overlapping strokes by pointer drag

log.note: deps set by the umbrella's planning run: pressing-b-picks-a-brush-that-paints-freehand-st

The user, 2026-10-24: 'watercolor doesn't look like watercolor'. Not built yet: DryMedia.swift:276 sends watercolour to the plain round tip until this task lands. The user also wants each brush's knobs to be the ones that make sense for that medium; Wetness and Bleed are the floor, add what a watercolourist expects (for example granulation, edge darkening) if it earns its place.

Adversarial review before building. (1) A Rebelle or Fresco user expects: a see-through wash, a darker rim where the wash dried, soft bleeding into damp paper, a cauliflower bloom when wet paint goes into a wash that has not dried, glazes that deepen where dry strokes cross, granulation in the paper, and a dry brush that skips on the tooth. All seven are buildable on the existing pixel engine (coverage fields, PaperGrain, the marker's multiply-over for live=landed). (2) Wet-on-wet needs time: strokes carry no time today, so a stroke gains an optional start time (seconds) recorded when the pointer goes down; old strokes have none and read as dry, so nothing already painted changes. (3) A real bloom lifts pigment out of the earlier wash (a pale middle). The live overlay can only lay paint over what is there (the smudge has the same limit), so the bloom is its new water spreading through the wet wash with a pale inside and a dark ragged front; the lift is a known departure, written in the design doc. (4) Wet-on-wet works within one Paint layer, which is where consecutive strokes land anyway (the first stroke makes the layer and picks it). (5) No mock draws watercolour; the bars decide the look. Settings: Wetness and Bleed, plus Granulation (a real watercolourist's choice: some pigments settle into the paper, some do not). Chose to keep edge darkening inside Wetness rather than a fourth knob because a dry brush genuinely has no pooled edge and a wet wash does, so one knob tells the truth.

Built: Watercolour.swift (wet-area/path depth fields, pooled edge, bleed fingers, granulation, dry brush, multiply glaze, blooms into washes still wet), BrushStroke.startedAt + drying, Granulation setting, live overlay replays the wet washes. Bars: edge-to-centre 1.41 (bar 1.3, round tip 1.00), spread past path 0.25 (bar 0.15, round tip -0.03); Bleed 0->100 spread 0.03->0.45; Wetness 0 leaves the tooth bare, 100 none. Walk watercolour-wash-and-bloom-walk (12 MP, no flags): moves 0.4-0.9 ms median, 1.8 ms worst; held vs landed 0.03-0.12% apart. Looked at: the stroke sheet (defaults read as mottled see-through washes with darker dried rims; wet crossings spread soft, dry ones are crisp glazes) and the walk's 5-glazed capture plus its close crop (left crossing spread sideways, right one a crisp darker square). Left rough, in the audit, not filed: bloom fronts break into flecks, dry brush blotches rather than streaks, Granulation 100 reads as dots, wet two-colour mixes a little muddy; the umbrella's blind test judges the look. Landing stall (~0.4 s per stroke at 12 MP, pencil too) folded into painting-keeps-up-with-the-pointer-on-a-12-megap. Chose Granulation as a third knob over an Edges knob because Wetness truthfully carries edge pooling.

Watercolour paints a see-through mottled wash pooled darker at its dried edge, creeping past the brush by Bleed, granulating (new Granulation setting), skipping as a dry brush at low Wetness, glazing where dry strokes cross, and blooming through washes still wet (strokes now record their start time; 1.5-8 s drying by Wetness). Sources/PhotonzRender/Watercolour.swift, live overlay replays the wet washes. Verified: 19 watercolour tests incl. bars edge-to-centre 1.41 (bar 1.3, round tip 1.00) and spread 0.25 (bar 0.15, round tip -0.03), live=landed; full suite 14500 green; walk watercolour-wash-and-bloom-walk on 12 MP with no flags: two crossings by pointer drag, moves 0.4-0.9 ms median, 1.8 ms worst.
